articles.author: Joe Jeneri
articles.description:
The Problem with GitHub Forks


If you've ever tried to find a meaningful contribution in a sea of repository forks on GitHub, you know the struggle. GitHub lists forks chronologically or simply alphabetically, often burying the most active and improved versions of a project under hundreds of stale copies.
When a project is abandoned or a community wants to take it in a new direction, the \"fork\" is the lifeblood of open source. But discovery is broken.
Before diving into our solution, we must acknowledge the tools that paved the way. Projects like Useful Forks and Active Forks have been the go-to resources for developers trying to make sense of the chaos. They provided the first real maps for the fork wilderness, and the community owes them a great debt.
At ForkFarm, we’re taking the next step. We don't just list forks; we rank them. Our goal is to help you find the \"true\" successor or the most improved version of any repository instantly.
What makes ForkFarm different?
Smart Ranking: We rank forks by stars, activity, and other health signals.
Visual Diff Highlights: We show you what actually changed compared to the upstream parent at a glance.
Deep Discovery: Whether it's a massive kernel or a small utility, we index the data that matters.
You can see how ForkFarm organizes massive ecosystems here:
Linux Kernel: forkfarm.cc/torvalds/linux - Find the most significant forks of the world's most famous repo.
Ollama: forkfarm.cc/ollama/ollama - Track how the AI community is expanding on the base project.
What signals do you value most when looking for a fork? Is it the number of commits ahead? The latest tag date? The star count of the fork itself?
We are actively refining our ranking algorithm and would love your input. We want ForkFarm to be the definitive tool for the open-source community to ensure that great code never stays buried.
Get in Touch
hello@forkfarm.cc.
Let's make open source more discoverable, one fork at a time.
articles.title: GitHub buries forks — ForkFarm ranks them
